take_homes: Reasoning for non-engineers: the knowledge has to be written down first, and that's what blocks a rollout more than the tools do
Ask whether a page could belong to a competitor, and require citations, to see if the agent used the memory or invented the answer
Put the style file and the rules file in the memory folder so every agent's output looks native to the company

monday.move: Pick one team outside engineering, probably sales, and have an agent draft a rules file and a style file from their Confluence space, proposal-only
monday.when: Monday morning, quick prototype before lunch
monday.stop_condition: stop if the sales lead doesn't read the output on their own after a week
monday.blocker: nobody in sales asked for it and I haven't decided who maintains it

misconception.why: The citations beat and the 'got sharper' beat were useful, but I took them as tricks to use, not as a reason to check output every time. The module still had me skip the plan review, and nothing there showed me output that looked fine and was wrong.

one_line: Good if your people have never built a memory, too slow if you already run agents, but the 'only what someone wrote down' point is the real one for a rollout.
